messages:
sam: quick heads-up — ran AWQ-int8 profile (awq-v0.9) with prefix-KV cache + continuous batching on the new sqaud-lite eval set. saw consistent ~3.8-4.2% EM drop vs float baseline, but ~18-22% token latency improvement. dumping notes.
jess: oof that's a big quality delta. did you run GPTQ baseline with same batch/cache config?
sam: yes — GPTQ-8bit w/ same runtime flags had ~0.9% EM drop and ~10% latency win. difference is larger when prefix cache hitrate > 40%.
kai: interesting. that implies AWQ interacts with KV cache semantics differently. any stack traces or anomalies in kv cache stats?
sam: kv-stats: `hits=4521, misses=6563, avg_kv_latency=0.8ms`. when hits>40% we see AWQ decode divergence more often. attached command I used:
```bash
./scripts/bakeoff.sh --model awq-v0.9 --quant awq --cache-prefix on --cont-batching on --eval sqaud-lite --runs 5
```
(no huge infra changes).
logan: can you paste a small example where outputs diverge? short QA pair maybe.
sam: pasted a pair below — baseline: "The capital is Paris." AWQ output: "The capital is" (truncated/misaligned). GPTQ preserves full answer.
maya: that looks like prefix-cache KV ordering + AWQ rounding is clipping KV contexts for certain head patterns. Might be microprecision causing next-token probs.
logan: any mismatch in kv checksum / seqhash?
sam: seqhash checks passed. but noticed microburst spikes in batch sizes during cont-batching: some batches jump to 16 tokens while most are 4. AWQ seems more sensitive to longer transient seqs.
jess: hypothesis: AWQ quant params tuned on average seq length; intermittent long batch sequences push quantized kernel into path that amplifies rounding error. we should try two things: 1) force batch cap to 8 and 2) disable prefix caching for hot routes and measure.
kai: agree. also run eval on summarization (XSum) — different distribution might hide/expose problem.
sam: started a gated run with batch_cap=8 and cache_prefix=off. job id: bake-22654-awq-01. infra-bot: deploy hook triggered for dedicated instance (ded-gpu-12) — log: deploy successful.
infra-bot: shadow traffic enabled on /v1/generate for model awq-v0.9 -> 10% weight, TTL=120s.
logan: cool. if revert is needed we should prioritize route-level fallback to GPTQ variant instead of full rollback. can we wire policy: if EM on eval drop > 2% then route fallback?
maya: yes we already have canary gating hooks. i'll add a quick eval check into the rollout job.
sam: interim numbers after 30m: batch_cap=8 + cache_off => EM drop reduced to ~1.2%, latency win drops to ~12%. putting these in sheet: https://go/rw/quant-batch-sheet (private).
jess: good trade. gid: run more runs on varied prompt lengths. also add token-level KL / logprob diffs to catch subtle hallucination changes.
kai: can we reproduce locally with `--no-net` harness? would speed iterate.
sam: yes, ran `harness/local_bake --model awq-v0.9 --no-net --seed 42` and saw same divergence patterns at scale.
logan: next actions: 1) expand evals (XSum, SQuAD, longform), 2) run AWQ retrain/tune on mixed sequence-length calibration set, 3) add runtime guard to cap batch growth during cont-batching for AWQ models.
maya: i'll own runtime guard (PR incoming), jess you own evaluation expansion, sam will run AWQ calibration.
jess: ack. thanks — will post concise results in #eng-ml after next pass. :thumbsup:
